sub_topic.description: 13-year academic progression (K-12) for Bible Translation Movements in The Renaissance & The Reformation (Roots of Individual Conscience) (History & Social Studies)

objectives.topic_name: The Renaissance & The Reformation (Roots of Individual Conscience)
objectives.objective_text: Explain how reformers translated the Bible into vernacular languages so ordinary people could read Scripture in their own tongue.

objectives.topic_name: The Renaissance & The Reformation (Roots of Individual Conscience)
objectives.objective_text: Describe the contributions of translators such as William Tyndale and Martin Luther, and the risks they faced in their work.

standards: C3 D2.His.3.9-12 — Use questions generated about individuals and groups to assess how the significance of their actions (history, grades 9-12)

objectives.topic_name: The Renaissance & The Reformation (Roots of Individual Conscience)
objectives.objective_text: Analyze the causes and effects of vernacular Bible translation on literacy, religious authority, and the spread of the Reformation.

standards: C3 D2.His.14.9-12 — Analyze multiple and complex causes and effects of events in the past (history, grades 9-12)

objectives.topic_name: The Renaissance & The Reformation (Roots of Individual Conscience)
objectives.objective_text: Assess how the significance of translators like Tyndale changed over time, from condemned heretics to celebrated shapers of language and faith.

standards: C3 D2.His.3.9-12 — Use questions generated about individuals and groups to assess how the significance of their actions (history, grades 9-12)

objectives.topic_name: The Renaissance & The Reformation (Roots of Individual Conscience)
objectives.objective_text: Evaluate how Bible translation movements were shaped by the printing press and the broader circumstances of Reformation Europe.

standards: C3 D2.His.1.9-12 — Evaluate how historical events and developments were shaped by unique circumstances of time and plac (history, grades 9-12)
